claim: BRCA1, BRCA2, and PALB2 proteins are tumor suppressors linked to a spectrum of malignancies, including breast cancer and Fanconi anemia.
source: BReast Cancer Associated proteins 1 and 2 (BRCA1, −2) and Partner and Localizer of BRCA2 (PALB2) protein are tumour suppressors linked to a spectrum of malignancies, including breast cancer and Fanconi anemia.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by established scientific knowledge about these proteins.

claim: PALB2 coordinates functions of BRCA1 and BRCA2 during homology-directed repair (HDR).
source: PALB2 coordinates functions of BRCA1 and BRCA2 during homology-directed repair (HDR) and interacts with several chromatin proteins.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract and is a known function of PALB2.

claim: PALB2 interacts with several chromatin proteins.
source: PALB2 coordinates functions of BRCA1 and BRCA2 during homology-directed repair (HDR) and interacts with several chromatin proteins.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: PALB2 binds DNA.
source: In addition to protein scaffold function, PALB2 binds DNA.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract and demonstrated throughout the manuscript.

claim: The functional role of PALB2 DNA binding is poorly understood.
source: The functional role of this interaction is poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as motivation for the study.

claim: Mutations in the PALB2 DNA-binding site reduce RAD51 foci formation by 50%.
source: We identified a major DNA-binding site of PALB2, mutations in which reduce RAD51 foci formation and the overall HDR efficiency in cells by 50%.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: Mutations in the PALB2 DNA-binding site reduce overall HDR efficiency in cells by 50%.
source: We identified a major DNA-binding site of PALB2, mutations in which reduce RAD51 foci formation and the overall HDR efficiency in cells by 50%.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3D.

claim: PALB2 N-terminal DNA-binding domain (N-DBD) stimulates the function of RAD51 recombinase.
source: PALB2 N-terminal DNA-binding domain (N-DBD) stimulates the function of RAD51 recombinase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 4 and Figure 5.

claim: PALB2 N-DBD possesses strand exchange activity without RAD51.
source: Surprisingly, it possesses the strand exchange activity without RAD51.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 4.

claim: PALB2 N-DBD stimulates inverse strand exchange.
source: Moreover, N-DBD stimulates the inverse strand exchange and can use DNA and RNA substrates.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 7.

claim: PALB2 N-DBD can use DNA and RNA substrates for strand exchange.
source: Moreover, N-DBD stimulates the inverse strand exchange and can use DNA and RNA substrates.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 7.

claim: PALB2 DNA binding plays a critical role for chromosome repair in cells.
source: Our data reveal a versatile DNA interaction property of PALB2 and demonstrate a critical role of PALB2 DNA binding for chromosome repair in cells.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by cellular assays in Figure 3.

claim: BRCA1 and BRCA2 regulate an efficient non-mutagenic pathway of chromosome break repair.
source: Breast cancer associated proteins 1 and 2 (BRCA1, −2) regulate an efficient non-mutagenic pathway of chromosome break repair and are described as guardians of chromosomal integrity (Venkitaraman, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: BRCA1 and BRCA2 initiate RAD51-mediated homologous recombination.
source: They initiate RAD51-mediated homologous recombination (HR) (Davies et al., 2001; Moynahan et al., 2001; Sharan et al., 1997; Venkitaraman, 2000)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations supporting the claim.

claim: BRCA1 and BRCA2 facilitate restart of stalled replication.
source: and facilitate restart of stalled replication (Badie et al., 2010; Lomonosov et al., 2003; Schlacher et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: BRCA2 belongs to a ubiquitous family of Recombination Mediator Proteins (RMPs).
source: BRCA2 belongs to a ubiquitous family of Recombination Mediator Proteins (RMPs), which stimulate formation of recombinase filament on single-stranded (ss) DNA protected by ssDNA-binding proteins, like SSB and RPA (Beernink and Morrical, 1999; Cox, 2007; Kowalczykowski, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the classification.

claim: PALB2 was discovered as a protein forming a complex with BRCA2 and regulating BRCA2 activity.
source: The Partner and Localizer of BRCA2 (PALB2) protein was discovered as a protein forming a complex with BRCA2 and regulating BRCA2 activity (Xia et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to the discovery paper.

claim: PALB2 is an essential mammalian protein linked to a similar spectrum of cancers and Fanconi anemia as BRCA proteins.
source: Like BRCA proteins, PALB2 is an essential mammalian protein linked to a similar spectrum of cancers and Fanconi anemia (Ducy et al., 2019; Pauty et al., 2014; Xia et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: The PALB2 C-terminal WD40 domain interacts with BRCA2.
source: The PALB2 C-terminal WD40 domain interacts with BRCA2 (Oliver et al., 2009; Xia et al., 2006)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the interaction.

claim: The PALB2 N-terminus forms a complex with BRCA1.
source: while the N-terminus forms a complex with BRCA1 (Zhang et al., 2009a; Zhang et al., 2009b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the interaction.

claim: BRCA1 localizes at double-stranded DNA break (DSB) sites at earlier stage of repair.
source: The latter localizes at double-stranded DNA break (DSB) sites at earlier stage of repair, inhibiting an alternative pathway of non-homologous end joining and initiating homology-directed repair (HDR) through recruitment of PALB2/BRCA2/RAD51 (Prakash et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: BRCA1 inhibits non-homologous end joining.
source: The latter localizes at double-stranded DNA break (DSB) sites at earlier stage of repair, inhibiting an alternative pathway of non-homologous end joining and initiating homology-directed repair (HDR) through recruitment of PALB2/BRCA2/RAD51 (Prakash et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: BRCA1 initiates homology-directed repair through recruitment of PALB2/BRCA2/RAD51.
source: The latter localizes at double-stranded DNA break (DSB) sites at earlier stage of repair, inhibiting an alternative pathway of non-homologous end joining and initiating homology-directed repair (HDR) through recruitment of PALB2/BRCA2/RAD51 (Prakash et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: PALB2 is often described as the hub for a network of tumor suppressors.
source: PALB2 is often described as the hub for a network of tumor suppressors (Park et al., 2014b; Sy et al., 2009b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the characterization.

claim: PALB2 contains a chromatin-association motif (ChAM) that interacts with histones H3 and H2B.
source: In addition to BRCA1 and −2 interactions, it contains a chromatin-association motif (ChAM) that interacts with histones H3 and H2B (Bleuyard et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the interaction.

claim: PALB2 binds MRG15 protein, a component of histone acetyltransferase-deacetylase complexes.
source: PALB2 binds MRG15 protein, a component of histone acetyltransferase-deacetylase complexes (Hayakawa et al., 2010; Sy et al., 2009a);
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the interaction.

claim: PALB2 binds RAD51 and its paralogs RAD51C, RAD51AP1 and XRCC3.
source: RAD51 and its paralogs RAD51C, RAD51AP1 and XRCC3 (Dray et al., 2010; Park et al., 2014a);
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the interactions.

claim: PALB2 binds translesion DNA polymerase η (Polη) during recombination-associated DNA synthesis.
source: translesion DNA polymerase η (Polη) during recombination-associated DNA synthesis (Buisson et al., 2014);
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the interaction.

claim: PALB2 binds an oxidative stress response protein KEAP1.
source: an oxidative stress response protein KEAP1 (Ma et al., 2012);
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the interaction.

claim: PALB2 binds RNF168 ubiquitin ligase.
source: and RNF168 ubiquitin ligase (Luijsterburg et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the interaction.

claim: PALB2 is ubiquitinylated in G1 phase of the cell cycle by KEAP1 and CUL3, leading to its degradation.
source: PALB2 is ubiquitinylated in G1 phase of the cell cycle by KEAP1 and CUL3, leading to its degradation, and, thereby, restraining its activity in S/G2 (Orthwein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: PALB2 is an RMP that promotes the assembly of RAD51-ssDNA presynaptic nucleofilaments in the absence of BRCA2 in vitro.
source: Furthermore, PALB2 is an RMP itself as it promotes the assembly of RAD51-ssDNA presynaptic nucleofilaments in the absence of BRCA2 in vitro (Buisson et al., 2010; Dray et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: PALB2 recruits Polη to DSB sites and stimulates recombination-associated DNA synthesis by Polη.
source: PALB2 recruits Polη to DSB sites and stimulates recombination-associated DNA synthesis by Polη (Buisson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: BRCA1, BRCA2 and PALB2 proteins contain DNA binding domains (DBDs), the function of which is poorly understood.
source: Apart from protein-protein interaction domains, BRCA1, −2 and PALB2 proteins also contain DNA binding domains (DBDs), the function of which is poorly understood (Buisson et al., 2010; Dray et al., 2010; Paull et al., 2001; Pellegrini et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: BRCA1/BARD1 complex plays a role in RAD51-mediated strand invasion and D-loop formation.
source: Recently, studies of BRCA1/BARD1 complex interaction with DNA and RAD51 led to the discovery of the BRCA1/BARD1 role in RAD51-mediated strand invasion and D-loop formation (Zhao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the discovery.

claim: Most missense mutations in the BRCA2 DBD are pathogenic.
source: Most missense mutations in the BRCA2 DBD are pathogenic (Guidugli et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Disruption of DNA binding in a BRCA2 truncation variant lacking the PALB2-binding motif leads to a significant HDR reduction.
source: Disruption of DNA binding in a BRCA2 truncation variant lacking the PALB2-binding motif leads to a significant HDR reduction (Siaud et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Deletion of the BRCA2 DBD has a negligible effect when interaction with PALB2 is preserved.
source: However, deletion of the BRCA2 DBD has a negligible effect when interaction with PALB2 is preserved, highlighting the functional importance of the previously reported DNA-binding property of PALB2 (Buisson et al., 2010; Dray et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Two truncation fragments of PALB2, T1 (residues 1–200) and T3 (residues 372–561), bind DNA.
source: Two truncation fragments of PALB2, T1 (residues 1–200) and T3 (residues 372–561), bind DNA (Buisson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: PALB2 truncation of 500 amino acids situated between the BRCA1 and BRCA2 binding motifs and containing both DBDs does not support BRCA2 and RAD51 foci formation in cells during DNA damage.
source: For example, PALB2 truncation of 500 amino acids situated between the BRCA1 and BRCA2 binding motifs and containing both DBDs does not support BRCA2 and RAD51 foci formation in cells during DNA damage (Sy et al., 2009b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the observation.

claim: The importance of DNA binding was demonstrated for other RMPs, including bacterial RecFOR.
source: The importance of DNA binding was demonstrated for other RMPs, including bacterial RecFOR (Korolev, 2017; Morimatsu and Kowalczykowski, 2003; Ryzhikov et al., 2014; Sakai and Cox, 2009; Umezu et al., 1993)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: The importance of DNA binding was demonstrated for eukaryotic RAD52.
source: and eukaryotic RAD52 (Arai et al., 2011; Seong et al., 2008).

source: T1 fragment alone interacts with all tested substrates with similar affinities as of PB2-573

claim: The T3 fragment has significantly lower affinity for DNA than T1 and PB2-573.
source: while the T3 fragment has significantly lower affinity for DNA

source: while that of the interaction of T3 with ss49 Kd(T3/ss49) is 484 ± 80 nM, which is likely an overestimation due to weak binding.

claim: Hill coefficient values for PALB2 fragment DNA binding are close to one, suggesting non-cooperative interactions.
source: Hill coefficient values are close to one, suggesting non-cooperative interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on the binding data.

claim: T1 binding to 49 bp dsDNA is cooperative.
source: The only exception is T1 binding to 49 bp dsDNA
evidence: This is stated in the results as an exception to the non-cooperative binding pattern.

claim: PB2-573 binding to 49 bp dsDNA is not cooperative.
source: however, the binding of PB2-573 to the same substrate is not cooperative.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

source: The only difference between T1 and PB2-573 was observed at an elevated salt concentration of 250 mM NaCl, where the PB2-573 fragment retained partial DNA binding activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).

claim: PALB2 DNA binding interactions are inhibited at 500 mM NaCl.
source: In both cases, interactions were inhibited by in 500 mM NaCl.

source: This suggests an interaction with ssDNA through multiple binding sites, potentially formed by the PALB2 oligomerization, as previously described (Buisson and Masson, 2012; Sy et al., 2009c), or through interaction with multiple binding sites within a monomer (see below).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the binding data and previous literature.

claim: N-DBD interaction with dsDNA is length-independent.
source: Interaction with dsDNA was length-independent, suggesting that more rigid dsDNA interacts with a single site.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on the binding data.

claim: The main DNA-binding cluster of PALB2 is formed by amino acids R146, R147, K148, and K149.
source: The main DNA-binding cluster is formed by amino acids R146, R147, K148, and K149.

source: Alanine substitution at these residues reduced binding affinity to ss49 by two orders of magnitude with a change in an apparent Kd from 4.0 ± 1.3 nM to 316 ± 59 nM in the case of N-DBD

claim: Alanine substitution at residues R146, R147, K148, and K149 reduced binding affinity to ss49 from 4.8 ± 0.4 nM to 187 ± 55 nM in PB2-573.

claim: PALB2 depletion leads to a severe defect in RAD51 foci formation.
source: PALB2 depletion leads to a severe defect in RAD51 foci formation.

source: WT PALB2 restores RAD51 foci formation

claim: The 146AAAA mutant interacts with RAD51 similarly to wild type PALB2.

claim: The cellular effect of the 146AAAA mutant is defined exclusively by the inability of PALB2 to interact with DNA.
source: Therefore, the cellular effect of the 146AAAA mutant is defined exclusively by the inability of PALB2 to interact with DNA.

claim: PALB2 DNA binding plays a critical role in HR and DNA repair in vivo.
source: Altogether, these studies show that PALB2 DNA binding plays a critical role in HR and DNA repair in vivo.

claim: Under solution conditions used in DNA-binding assays, RAD51 displayed low activity.

claim: The N-DBD promotes strand exchange at a comparable rate even without RAD51.
source: Surprisingly, the N-DBD promotes strand exchange at a comparable rate even without RAD51.

source: The strand exchange activity was not observed by full length PALB2 in previous publications (Buisson et al., 2010; Dray et al., 2010).

source: This difference could be due to significantly lower concentrations of PALB2 used in the referred studies as well as different experimental conditions.

source: and the maximum rate of strand exchange is reached at 1 μM of N-DBD.
